Pay attention to

gaps, not silently inferred requirements.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree completed by enrollment permits direct PhD application; full-time study only. Minimum
background: three calculus semesters including advanced calculus or linear algebra; actual preparation is
normally greater. UChicago bachelor’s and international status are compatible with application; GSAS explicitly
considers applicants irrespective of citizenship. [s1] [s7]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD in GSAS (not Tandon); only one GSAS application per term. Gather transcripts, three
references and subject GRE or short impossibility explanation. Resolve conflicting January dates with
admissions@math.nyu.edu before submission. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No pre-application advisor agreement listed. Five direct matches below follow official research groups; recent
metadata verified for Pirutka, Tosatti, Tschinkel, but Bogomolov/Cappell official pages are stale. Ask about
active supervision and availability. [s12] [s13]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Public application page specifies one GSAS application per term and all supporting items by deadline. Scores
missing from postsubmission checklist can be traced through dedicated official score-check form. Detailed
help/statements pages were blocked. [s2] [s14] [s8]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027 evidence exists for NYU Shanghai Mathematics; New York Courant main page remains yearless and
disagrees by two days. Funding amount is prior-year 2026-27 only. [s1] [s5] [s6]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Conflict]
Unresolved conflict: Courant lists January 4 without year; NYU Shanghai’s same GSAS Mathematics PhD
process expressly lists January 6, 2027 for Fall 2027. Do not silently transfer Shanghai’s date to New York.
Treat January 4 as the conservative planning date, with year/timezone unconfirmed; request written New York
confirmation. [s1] [s6]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Department says applications must arrive January 4 for MacCracken consideration; major review early
February. No current-year separate deadline established; same January conflict applies. [s3] [s6]

Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Conflict]
GSAS requires application, uploads, official scores and letters by the applicable program deadline; no grace
period promised. Exact New York date is unresolved (department January 4 annual versus Shanghai January 6,
2027). [s2] [s1] [s6]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No 2027 reply deadline established from accessible Courant/GSAS admissions/funding sources. Obtain date in
admission/funding offer; do not infer April 15 from an older resolution. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Department names TOEFL or IELTS for applicants without native English or an English-medium
bachelor’s/master’s. GSAS guidance reproduced by another department recommends TOEFL 100 (old scale) or
IELTS 7; current GSAS English page was inaccessible, so new test-scale thresholds and acceptance of DET
require verification. [s1] [s10]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Completed UChicago English-medium bachelor’s fits departmental degree exemption. Whether an in-progress
degree qualifies at submission and whether evidence/waiver form is required could not be verified centrally;
confirm if not yet conferred. F-1 status alone is not the exemption. [s1] [s8]
GRE General [Conflict]
Admissions policy: neither required nor accepted. Funding page incorrectly/olderly says general and subject
optional; follow specific admissions policy pending confirmation. [s1] [s3]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Admissions policy expects Math Subject GRE; if impractical, attach short explanatory statement. Funding page
says optional for all PhD applications; conflicting official pages. ETS institution 2596, GRE department 0703. [s1]
[s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2026-27 GSAS doctoral base stipend USD 37,132 for the academic year (USD 18,566/semester), not a verified
2027-28 Courant offer. MacCracken covers nine months plus tuition, registration fees and individual
comprehensive health insurance. February 2026 math guidebook says no general departmental/GSAS summer
allocation; summer grant, teaching or internship support must be separately arranged. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Years of support [Standing rule]
MacCracken renewable up to five years with satisfactory progress; competitive merit award, not a public
guarantee to every applicant. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants use same deadline and are not excluded by merit-based MacCracken description.
Exact offer and any outside award citizenship condition control; federal need-based aid should not be assumed
available to F-1 students. [s1] [s3] [s7]
Conditions and duties [Prior cycle]
MacCracken itself has no teaching requirement according to February 2026 guidebook; teaching can provide
extra pay. Summer grants depend on advisor/project; internships require independently arranged placement
and appropriate CPT/OPT authorization. [s4]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
MacCracken review uses incoming full-time PhD application. No separate MacCracken essay/reference
requirement found; exact scholarship short-answer fields not verified in blocked GSAS portal help. [s3] [s8]

Other funding routes [Standing rule]
External fellowships encouraged, with possible departmental supplementation of lower stipends; need-based
aid is a distinct route with eligibility not established for this applicant. Summer advisor grants, teaching and
internships are conditional options. [s3] [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 110 listed in official NYU Journalism instructions for the same GSAS application; current mathematics
portal amount not independently accessible, so verify before payment. [s10]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
GSAS-specific current eligibility, international hardship rules, request method and lead time were not publicly
retrievable after targeted searches. Contact gsas.admissions@nyu.edu before paying/submitting; do not use
Tandon/Steinhardt waiver policies. [s8]

text:
New York University - Courant Institute
United States · Mathematics PhD
2026 US News roster/rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• New York deadline and GRE rules conflict across official pages; resolve before relying on them.
• Nine-month MacCracken funding does not guarantee summer funding.
• Central GSAS website access blocked exact writing and referee instructions; these are explicit unresolved
gaps, not silently inferred requirements.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree completed by enrollment permits direct PhD application; full-time study only. Minimum
background: three calculus semesters including advanced calculus or linear algebra; actual preparation is
normally greater. UChicago bachelor’s and international status are compatible with application; GSAS explicitly
considers applicants irrespective of citizenship. [s1] [s7]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD in GSAS (not Tandon); only one GSAS application per term. Gather transcripts, three
references and subject GRE or short impossibility explanation. Resolve conflicting January dates with
admissions@math.nyu.edu before submission. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No pre-application advisor agreement listed. Five direct matches below follow official research groups; recent
metadata verified for Pirutka, Tosatti, Tschinkel, but Bogomolov/Cappell official pages are stale. Ask about
active supervision and availability. [s12] [s13]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Public application page specifies one GSAS application per term and all supporting items by deadline. Scores
missing from postsubmission checklist can be traced through dedicated official score-check form. Detailed
help/statements pages were blocked. [s2] [s14] [s8]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027 evidence exists for NYU Shanghai Mathematics; New York Courant main page remains yearless and
disagrees by two days. Funding amount is prior-year 2026-27 only. [s1] [s5] [s6]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Conflict]
Unresolved conflict: Courant lists January 4 without year; NYU Shanghai’s same GSAS Mathematics PhD
process expressly lists January 6, 2027 for Fall 2027. Do not silently transfer Shanghai’s date to New York.
Treat January 4 as the conservative planning date, with year/timezone unconfirmed; request written New York
confirmation. [s1] [s6]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Department says applications must arrive January 4 for MacCracken consideration; major review early
February. No current-year separate deadline established; same January conflict applies. [s3] [s6]

Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Conflict]
GSAS requires application, uploads, official scores and letters by the applicable program deadline; no grace
period promised. Exact New York date is unresolved (department January 4 annual versus Shanghai January 6,
2027). [s2] [s1] [s6]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No 2027 reply deadline established from accessible Courant/GSAS admissions/funding sources. Obtain date in
admission/funding offer; do not infer April 15 from an older resolution. [s1] [s2]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Department names TOEFL or IELTS for applicants without native English or an English-medium
bachelor’s/master’s. GSAS guidance reproduced by another department recommends TOEFL 100 (old scale) or
IELTS 7; current GSAS English page was inaccessible, so new test-scale thresholds and acceptance of DET
require verification. [s1] [s10]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Completed UChicago English-medium bachelor’s fits departmental degree exemption. Whether an in-progress
degree qualifies at submission and whether evidence/waiver form is required could not be verified centrally;
confirm if not yet conferred. F-1 status alone is not the exemption. [s1] [s8]
GRE General [Conflict]
Admissions policy: neither required nor accepted. Funding page incorrectly/olderly says general and subject
optional; follow specific admissions policy pending confirmation. [s1] [s3]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Admissions policy expects Math Subject GRE; if impractical, attach short explanatory statement. Funding page
says optional for all PhD applications; conflicting official pages. ETS institution 2596, GRE department 0703. [s1]
[s3]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload institution-issued official transcript from every previously attended institution, including
graduate/continuing study. GSAS guidance says current academic record if degree incomplete; no paper copies
when uploaded, final official transcript after offer. [s1] [s10]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separate course list/descriptions specified in accessible math admissions page; current program
supplement must be checked for required/optional status, fields and upload rules. [s1] [s8]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three electronic letters; strongly recommended that at least two be mathematics/science course instructors.
[s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
MacCracken review uses incoming full-time PhD application. No separate MacCracken essay/reference
requirement found; exact scholarship short-answer fields not verified in blocked GSAS portal help. [s3] [s8]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Online letters required, but precise GSAS trigger (registration versus separate send button; before versus only
after submission) not publicly verified because central help was access-blocked. Do not borrow Tandon or
Steinhardt mechanics. [s1] [s8]

Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Department points applicants to GSAS verification of receipt; GSAS has an Application Checklist (confirmed for
test scores). Exact letter statuses/email confirmations were not accessible. [s1] [s14]
Updating and reusing letters [Prior cycle]
Older GSAS policy requires a new application and all supporting credentials on reapplication. Current
same-cycle letter replacement/FERPA/reuse rules not verified; ask GSAS before assuming portability. [s11] [s8]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume; Statement of purpose; Personal / background statement; Research-interest
statement; Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list
[Unresolved]
Exact current Mathematics required/optional status, prompt, length/format and upload-versus-link rule were
not established: public math checklist is incomplete and GSAS statements/resource-center pages returned
access errors. Retrieve current application instructions before drafting; do not import another NYU school’s
requirements. [s1] [s8] [s9]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate course list/descriptions specified in accessible math admissions page; current program
supplement must be checked for required/optional status, fields and upload rules. [s1] [s8]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
MacCracken review uses incoming full-time PhD application. No separate MacCracken essay/reference
requirement found; exact scholarship short-answer fields not verified in blocked GSAS portal help. [s3] [s8]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Short GRE-impracticality explanation required when omitting expected Math Subject score; no public exact
prompt, length cap or formatting beyond short statement attached to application. [s1]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2026-27 GSAS doctoral base stipend USD 37,132 for the academic year (USD 18,566/semester), not a verified
2027-28 Courant offer. MacCracken covers nine months plus tuition, registration fees and individual
comprehensive health insurance. February 2026 math guidebook says no general departmental/GSAS summer
allocation; summer grant, teaching or internship support must be separately arranged. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Years of support [Standing rule]
MacCracken renewable up to five years with satisfactory progress; competitive merit award, not a public
guarantee to every applicant. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants use same deadline and are not excluded by merit-based MacCracken description.
Exact offer and any outside award citizenship condition control; federal need-based aid should not be assumed
available to F-1 students. [s1] [s3] [s7]
Conditions and duties [Prior cycle]
MacCracken itself has no teaching requirement according to February 2026 guidebook; teaching can provide
extra pay. Summer grants depend on advisor/project; internships require independently arranged placement
and appropriate CPT/OPT authorization. [s4]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
MacCracken review uses incoming full-time PhD application. No separate MacCracken essay/reference
requirement found; exact scholarship short-answer fields not verified in blocked GSAS portal help. [s3] [s8]

Other funding routes [Standing rule]
External fellowships encouraged, with possible departmental supplementation of lower stipends; need-based
aid is a distinct route with eligibility not established for this applicant. Summer advisor grants, teaching and
internships are conditional options. [s3] [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 110 listed in official NYU Journalism instructions for the same GSAS application; current mathematics
portal amount not independently accessible, so verify before payment. [s10]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
GSAS-specific current eligibility, international hardship rules, request method and lead time were not publicly
retrievable after targeted searches. Contact gsas.admissions@nyu.edu before paying/submitting; do not use
Tandon/Steinhardt waiver policies. [s8]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Main admissions page expects subject GRE and rejects General; funding page says both optional. Main New
York January 4 annual deadline differs from Shanghai explicit January 6, 2027. Central help could not settle
these. [s1] [s3] [s6]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Highest priority: confirm New York 2027 deadline/timezone and GRE policy; retrieve exact
statement/CV/course supplement; confirm fee/waiver and referee triggers/replacement; verify in-progress
English-degree exemption and 2027-28 stipend/summer terms; ask which listed faculty are taking students.
